chunks: Those who accepted the faith and left their homes and fought by your side, are your brothers; yet those who are related by blood are closer to one another according to the decree of God. Verily God knows everything.

key_terms.إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ: Verily God is All-Knowing of everything
key_terms.فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: According to the decree of God

ai.seo_question: Who are closer to each other in inheritance: those of faith or blood relatives?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for establishing the dual hierarchy of *Nasab* (lineage) and *Iman* (faith), particularly clarifying that blood relatives retain priority in inheritance even after the advent of Islam, a principle upheld by the Imams. It underscores the continuity of pre-Islamic kinship ties within the divine legal framework, affirming that while Muhajirun and Ansar are brothers in faith, the specific rights of kinship (*Ulu al-Arham*) are preserved as a distinct divine decree.
